author: reek
body: Every other operation the compute bridge serves is computed by the emulator on the host CPU, in scalar C. This one is not: the module below is handed to the CUDA driver, compiled for whatever card is present, and launched. That is the difference between a bridge that dispatches and a bridge that pretends to.

author: reek
body: THE ARITHMETIC IS CHOSEN SO THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD HAVE PRODUCED IT. The kernel computes ten times the input plus five, which no operation in the host's scalar table computes, over an input whose values are 1, 2, 3 and 4. The answers are 15, 25, 35 and 45: four distinct numbers, none of them an input, none of them a permutation of the inputs, and none reachable by echoing the operand buffer back.

author: reek
body: TWO CONTROLS, AND THEY ARE THE POINT. A test that only ever sees the kernel succeed cannot tell a driver that compiled and ran the module from a host that answered a canned reply.

author: reek
body: A box with no NVIDIA GPU refuses all three, and this test then FAILS rather than skipping. That is deliberate: a skip reads as coverage, and the claim being made here is about hardware. A failure that names the missing device is the honest answer on a machine that does not have one.
